questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My heritage as I went to Beijing and my parents are Chinese, and I speak the language. Also because the university is highly ranked.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had such a nice experience overall. If you are curious and willing to put the effort, its a great opportunity to be familiar with a different culture.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: From a exchange coordinator

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Some courses were not accessible

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Buildings with AB rooms (shared bathroom) or double rooms (shared with one person) for 40 RNB pr. day. Buildings with single rooms for 80 RNB pr. day.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared kitchen spaces in the buildings. A lot canteens on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its really good!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are different rounds. First round you sign up for courses within your department. The popular courses get filled out fast. Second round you sign up for courses out of your department. You can drop courses until some weeks later.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Exchange coordinators etc. Not that much help which was a bit frustrating. No introduction really to the system.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: No as some courses were not offered to exchange students and some were not offered in English, even though it seem that way from the course catalogue. No consistency really with the catalogue and the courses in the portal, which is stressful as they get filled up quickly.  However, for the existing courses that were open for exchange students, the coordinators were in most cases able to open up extra spots for the students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry about finding the courses beforehand too much as they deviate from what is really offered.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Different levels. Some were harder as Corporate Finance. Some were easier, as they only graded on a book report, homework and a presentation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Really different in the grading system as the grades are splitted into different percentages for different test methods (homework, test, presentation, attendance).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Corporate Finance, Macroeconomic Analysis, Health Economics, Labor Economics, Developmental Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Corporate Finance, as it was harder and you therefore learned more. Health Economics was also interesting. Easy to pass, but interesting course.

questions.answer: Its pretty cheap. Especially food and taxis.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot! However, some were not relevant for students not speaking chinese.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Football! Its fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Clubs, go out for dinner, travel to different cities via. high-speed train or plane.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The local students are really different, as chinese students tend to make their life more about school.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: China is not easy to survive in, in terms of payments and practical stuff. You have to be willing to do the effort. Also do some research beforehand, as you need to be familiar with the apps. Everything is automated, so all payment process is via QR code etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Its a nice university.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met on exchange. All are very ambitious as it is a highly ranked university. Also curious about China, which I believe is great.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That its difficult to adapt to the pratical processes as payments etc. and people are not familiar with english. However, if you're interested of a different culture, I think its a part of the experience!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I loved the experience as a whole!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
